topics: Exec readout agenda and success criteria
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-28
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 55 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Priya Rao (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Oscar Gomez (Questing Head of ML), Nina Patel (Questing Director of Platform), Samir Khatri (Questing Security), Leah Brooks (Product)
Shared artefacts: drive.redwood/questing-poc (SOW draft), bench-plan.xlsx, access-checklist.md

[00:00] Priya Rao: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick intro, I'm Priya, AE on the account, Marcus is our solutions engineer, Oscar, Nina, thanks for carving the time.
[00:12] Oscar Gomez: Yeah thanks, and hi folks — trying to keep this focused. We want to make sure this POC actually proves two things: latency is predictable at scale, and we can save on per-token cost versus our current self-hosted fleet.
[00:25] Marcus Li: Perfect. We'll run through a proposed sprint matrix today: kickoff, access/ingest, midpoint benchmark, and then an exec readout. Also discuss success criteria and gating.
[00:38] Nina Patel: Quick note on timeline constraints — we have an internal exec offsite first week of April so ideally readout before that.
[00:45] Priya Rao: Ok noted, so that pushes a tighter mid-March midpoint.
[00:50] Samir Khatri: From security, we need to confirm KMS and audit log retention; also SSO — SAML, not OIDC for now.
[00:58] Marcus Li: That’s fine. We'll supply an IAM template and KMS integration guide. For SAML we have a standard IdP SAML flow.
[01:10] Oscar Gomez: For the workloads — three interactive endpoints: 1) triage-chat (avg seq len 120 tokens), 2) summarization (avg 400 tokens), 3) clinical question-answering (avg 220 tokens). Plus an embedding batch job nightly ~50k docs. QPS distribution: 70% triage-chat low latency, 20% QA medium, 10% summarization.
[01:30] Marcus Li: Good detail. We'll size the POC load: 50 concurrent chat sessions, sustained 5 QPS for triage-chat with bursts to 20 QPS in spikes for 30s. Embedding batch we'll simulate with your object sizes.
[01:45] Priya Rao: Success criteria proposal: 95th percentile latency under 250ms for triage-chat when under sustained load, cost per 1M tokens less than current baseline by 20%, and no PII leakage in logs. Thoughts?
[01:58] Leah Brooks: The exec cares about cost and reliability; 250ms 95th seems aggressive but if you can demonstrate headroom that's compelling.
[02:10] Oscar Gomez: We can agree to that but want to see the exact benchmarking method — how you're accounting for prefix caching and batching — because our current infra uses some custom KV caching.
[02:22] Marcus Li: We'll document the bench harness — explicitly show settings: batching window, cache TTL, quantization model variants. We'll run with/without caching to show delta.
[02:33] Nina Patel: Access — who needs what? We can't give production data, but we can provide sanitized samples and API keys for staging. We need to know the network setup for Private vs Hosted modes too.
[02:46] Priya Rao: Two paths: 1) Hosted Redwood API with VPC peering and private networking for data egress controls, or 2) Private deployment in your VPC — that one will take longer (setup and approvals). For a 4-week POC we recommend Hosted with VPC peering to meet timeline.
[03:05] Samir Khatri: If we do Hosted, we need proof that logs are encrypted at rest and a KMS integration. Also retention policy must be configurable.
[03:13] Marcus Li: We have KMS integration and can redact logs; we'll provide SOC2 artifacts and the retention settings.
[03:20] Oscar Gomez: Benchmarks — please include both latency and token-level cost breakdowns. For latency include p50, p95, p99 and tail latency graphs. Also measure cold-start for stateful sessions.
[03:33] Marcus Li: Cold-start meaning KV cache warmup? We'll instrument kv-hit rates and report warm/cold runs.
[03:41] Leah Brooks: Mid-point review — what constitutes a pass?
[03:45] Priya Rao: Mid-point pass gate recommended: 1) ability to reproduce triage-chat p95 < 300ms in staging, 2) benchmark harness showing cost trends and expected unit economics, 3) access and logs validated by security. If any gate fails we do a 7-day mitigation sprint.
[03:59] Oscar Gomez: Ok that seems reasonable. We want the exec readout to contain a clear ask: either scale to dedicated or continue hosted with committed units.
[04:09] Priya Rao: We'll prepare a 10-slide exec deck template: objectives, test results, cost delta, operational checklist, and recommended next step.
[04:18] Nina Patel: Timeline check — you said 4 weeks, can you break down weeks?
[04:22] Marcus Li: Week 0 (this week) — kickoff + access; Week 1 — ingest sample data and smoke tests; Week 2 — full benchmark runs and tuning; Week 3 — mid-point review and re-runs as needed; Week 4 — consolidation and exec readout prep.
[04:38] Oscar Gomez: We might need two days for legal to sign the minimal DPA for staging access.
[04:43] Samir Khatri: Also include a short runbook for suspected PII hits — auto-redact and notification flow.
[04:50] Marcus Li: Will include runbook and an evidence capture procedure for security review.
[04:54] Priya Rao: Let’s capture immediate action items — I'll email SOW and access checklist; Marcus will drop bench-plan.xlsx and run the dry-run; Oscar will upload sample payloads to the secure share.
[05:06] Nina Patel: For benchmarking, we also want cost per 1M tokens and per-endpoint cost attribution. Can you break out tokenization differences between models?
[05:18] Marcus Li: Yep, we’ll include tokenization delta and model variant cost table (float16 vs int8 quantized variants).
[05:25] Leah Brooks: Any concerns about model fidelity? We have an internal eval harness, might want to run quality regression tests too.
[05:32] Marcus Li: We'll run a small eval set and surface any accuracy regressions; also tie quality monitoring to rollbacks in the readout.
[05:39] Oscar Gomez: Who's responsible for scheduling the mid-point review?
[05:42] Priya Rao: Priya will propose two slots; customer picks. We tentatively proposed week of 2025-03-24.
[05:49] Samir Khatri: And the exec readout — we target 2025-04-04 as Nina said earlier?
[05:53] Nina Patel: That's ideal yes.
[05:55] Priya Rao: Great. Any other blockers?
[05:58] Oscar Gomez: None from me; just need the SOW and the checklist.
[06:01] Marcus Li: I'll run the dry-run benchmark on Thursday and share results in the shared sheet. Expect initial numbers for p50/p95 and cost per 100k tokens.
[06:11] Leah Brooks: Please make sure the exec deck includes recommended next-step ask and estimated committed spend.
[06:16] Priya Rao: Will do. Thanks everyone — we’ll follow up with the SOW and scheduling.
[06:20] Oscar Gomez: Thanks, talk soon.

Meeting end.
